stem: Copper is used in electrical equipment. It has a melting point of $1085^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Identify the lattice structure of copper.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Draw a labelled diagram to show the bonding present in copper.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The relative isotopic masses and natural abundances of the two isotopes in a sample of copper are shown in Table 1.1.

**Table 1.1**

| isotope | relative isotopic mass | % abundance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $^{63}\text{Cu}$ | 62.930 | 69.15 |
| $^{65}\text{Cu}$ | 64.928 | 30.85 |
parts.text: Define the unified atomic mass unit.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Define relative atomic mass, $A_{\text{r}}$, in terms of the unified atomic mass unit.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Calculate the relative atomic mass, $A_{\text{r}}$, of copper in this sample using the data in Table 1.1.

Show your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The mass spectrum of a sample of pure copper is shown in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

**Fig. 1.1**

Identify the ion with an abundance of 23% in the sample.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
When $\text{KI}\text{(aq)}$ is added to $\text{CuSO}_{4}\text{(aq)}$ the blue-coloured solution turns brown and a white precipitate of $\text{CuI}\text{(s)}$ is seen.

The reaction between copper ions and iodide forms only two products.
parts.text:
Complete the equation for this reaction.

$$\ldots\ldots\text{Cu}^{2+} + \ldots\ldots\text{I}^- \rightarrow \ldots\ldots\text{CuI} + \ldots\ldots\ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the oxidising agent in this reaction. Explain your answer in terms of electron transfer.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: State the full electronic configuration of $\text{Cu}^{2+}$.
